verdictStatement: The subject's central honesty repair is real in substance and unwarranted in provenance. lockJoin's widened no-lock rule is faithfully supported by component-manifest-schemas.v6 at that artifact's own bytes — I verified it clause by clause — but the sentence that carries it into recordedInputs attributes the same width to 'the accepted v2 contract', and the accepted v2 contract does not hold it. Separately, the artifact publishes two change manifests of its own v1→v2 delta that are not co-extensive, and neither names the change it made to authorityClaim. Everything the dispatch told me to attack that is NOT in the finding list below, I attacked and failed to break: the verbatim carries are byte-exact, the surface list is honest, S-EVIDENCE is genuinely deferred, the extra rows are genuinely not self-admitted, numeric windows are genuinely unfilled, schemas.v6 is correctly candidate-marked, and nothing in the artifact claims SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, or implementation authorization.

blockers.title: The honesty repair borrows D-013's acceptance for a width the accepted contract does not hold
blockers.subjectQuote: v6 (and the accepted v2 contract) state that NO lock of any form is producible until DR-111 closes.

measurement.referentIdentified: 'the accepted v2 contract' resolves to component-manifest-schemas.v2.json. D-013 (ADOPTED 2026-08-13, 'DR-103: the accepted manifest/index/lock design contract') records that artifact as DR-103's accepted design contract at 73114ddec12d3ec6dfbcb51b7002d983ff9dbfa1fa39189bb025008f1f501381. I measured the file: it is still those bytes. The referent is real, unambiguous, and genuinely accepted — I checked this before concluding anything, because the opposite reading (that 'accepted' was itself false) would have been the easier finding and it is not the true one.
measurement.whatTheAcceptedContractActuallySays: component-manifest-schemas.v2 /identityDependencies/dependencies[3] (ID-DEP-4), verbatim: '... so until DR-111 closes no lock over a CONSTRAINED REQUEST is producible at all.' Its /lockSchema/fields[1]/type admits one request form only — 'the resolved dependency roots as (stableId, versionConstraint) pairs'. Exact-pin is not a form in that document at all, so v2 could not and did not rule on it. Its /lockSchema/purpose carries no no-lock clause whatsoever.
measurement.whereTheWiderClaimActuallyComesFrom: Only from component-manifest-schemas.v6, and only after four rounds of author-initiated oscillation recorded in v6's own repairLog: [17] exact-pin declared producible, [21] narrowed to dependency-free single components, [22] a v3 reversion of v2's A5 flagged as undisclosed, [27] widened to 'no lock is producible until DR-111, including exact-pin requests of any cardinality', [28] widened again to the compatibility grounds the subject now quotes. v6 repairLog[24] records in its own words that 'ID-DEP-4-LOCK-PRODUCIBILITY was author-initiated, not a verdict finding'. v6 is a candidate; no coordinator decision records it; it has passed no acceptance gate.

blockers.whyBlocker: The subject widens the accepted contract's holding from 'no lock over a constrained request' to 'NO lock of any form' and presents the wider proposition as jointly held by the accepted document. A coordinator reading this sentence would conclude that the widest lock prohibition already carries D-013's acceptance behind it. It does not — it carries only an unaccepted candidate's author-initiated amendment. This is the mirror image of the failure mode the dispatch names as 'treating schemas.v6 as accepted': the subject does not call v6 accepted, it launders v6's width through the artifact that is. And it does so inside the single sentence that replaced v1's dishonest sentence, in the field the artifact bills as its principal honesty repair — which is precisely where a borrowed warrant does the most damage.
blockers.notARequestToWeakenTheRule: lockJoin's substance is independently sound and I do not ask for it to be softened. v6 genuinely says what the subject says v6 says (M-11). The defect is the parenthetical, not the rule.
blockers.minimumRepair: Attribute each width to its actual holder. E.g.: 'v6 states that NO lock of any form — exact-pin or constrained, any cardinality — is producible until DR-111 closes. The D-013-accepted component-manifest-schemas.v2 (73114dde…) states the narrower rule that no lock over a constrained request is producible; the widening to exact-pin and to cardinality is v6's and is author-initiated, not yet accepted. Citing v6 does not accept it.' Any repair that keeps a single sentence attributing one width to both documents reproduces the defect.

measurement.honestyRepairsFromV1Names: lockJoin and the recordedInputs schemas.v3 role sentence (item 1); the v3→v6 citation repoint (item 2); a negative assertion about what did not change (item 3). It does NOT name authorityClaim, purpose, or reviewGuidance.
measurement.basedOnMethodNames: 'lockJoin, schemas citation, reviewGuidance'. It does NOT name authorityClaim or purpose. Its qualifier is absolute: 'v2 is v1 with targeted honesty repairs ONLY'.

measurement.theTwoManifestsDisagree: reviewGuidance is named by basedOn.method and not by honestyRepairsFromV1. The artifact therefore ships two non-co-extensive accounts of its own delta, and its reviewGuidance directs the reviewer to bound the diff by honestyRepairsFromV1 — the weaker of the two.

theUndisclosedText.authorityClaim: v2 inserts 'does not make any lock producible by itself (DR-103 lock production still waits on this row closing AND a later DR-103 successor that consumes the windows),'
theUndisclosedText.purpose: v2 inserts 'and states that NO DR-103 lock of any form is producible until this row closes with evaluable windows (plus the closure/compatibility meaning DR-103 ID-DEP-4 names)'

blockers.whyBlocker: I record plainly that both insertions NARROW rather than expand — read on their merits they are honest, and a coordinator may reasonably weigh that in downgrading this finding. What makes it blocker-grade is method, not content. This lane's review is a bounded-diff review: the artifact's own reviewGuidance instructs 'Attack any silent v1-to-v2 change outside honestyRepairsFromV1', and the sibling lineage states the bar absolutely ('Every v4-to-v5 path the v5 repairLog does not name must be byte-identical to v4', component-manifest-schemas.v6 reviewGuidance). A coordinator who bounds their re-read by the manifest would not re-read authorityClaim — the one field that states what the artifact claims authority to do. An incomplete manifest on that field defeats the method the artifact asks to be reviewed by, and the defect is self-certifying: the same lineage already recorded an undisclosed change as a finding (v6 repairLog[22], 'v3 reverts the closure-rule half of v2 A5 without disclosing the removal'). Publishing two manifests that disagree with each other compounds it.
blockers.minimumRepair: Make one manifest authoritative and complete. It must name authorityClaim and purpose as changed, quote or point at the inserted clauses, and either fold basedOn.method into it or make the two identical in extent. The negative assertion (item 3 / 'No surface list, six-cell, or bridge-meaning change') is measurably true and should be kept.

A slice-1 scoping cell should not rest on vocabulary from an artifact that has not been reviewed at all.

shouldFix.title: recordedInputs.governingSources omits every load-bearing source except three
shouldFix.measurement: Digested somewhere in the artifact: file 04 (twice), file 08 (inside registerRowQuoted), COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, component-manifest-schemas.v6. Load-bearing but carrying no digest and, in most cases, no path anywhere in the artifact: (a) docs/v2/architecture/02-distribution-and-components.md L164-165 — the verbatim must-not that bridgesMean rests on, cited only as 'file 02 must-not'; (b) docs/coop/artifacts/dr-202.re-review-independent.json — cited only as 'DR-202 F3'; the finding's actual id is DR202-RR-F3 and its status is ADVISORY / STANDS-AS-ROUTED, which the subject does not say; (c) control-protocol-contract.v2.json — S-CTRL consumes its row skeleton (M-17); D-015-accepted at c50a79fe…, matching current bytes; (d) doctor-contract.v4.json and sarif-projection-contract.v1.json — the two proposed extra rows; (e) file 09 L41 / delivery.v4.json — the warrant for S-TS1's 'applied delivery major 1'; (f) state-class-contract.v1.json, per S-1.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Every one of these claims checks out — I verified all six against primary bytes and none is fabricated. That is exactly why the gap is worth fixing rather than fatal: the artifact is right and cannot be shown to be right from its own recorded inputs. A later reader re-measuring this contract can re-measure three of its nine sources. The lineage's own standard is digest-and-line citation for anything load-bearing, and the subject meets that standard for the sources it happens to list.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add the six sources to governingSources with path, sha256 and a one-line role. For (b), name the finding by its real id DR202-RR-F3, its file, and its ADVISORY standing, noting that file 08's DR-202 row is what routes it to the DR-111 closure — that route is the strongest warrant the subject has for S-EVIDENCE and it currently goes uncited.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the surface list is not closed: the artifact calls it 'the closed surface list for this closure' while holding S-DOCTOR and S-SARIF in abeyance. Not a defect — 'for this closure' is the correct scoping and the proposals are marked not-admitted.

That leaving S-ROLE RESERVED and S-EVIDENCE DEFERRED means the artifact cannot close a row whose acceptance cell demands per-surface matrices. Disclosed, not smuggled: the artifact denies SATISFYING DR-111, and DR202-RR-F3's routed remedy is precisely a D-002-style scoped closure.

That 'the accepted v2 contract' has no resolvable referent, or falsely claims acceptance. Both false: D-013 accepts component-manifest-schemas.v2 and its digest still matches. The real defect is narrower and is B-1.
That S-STATE drags an inherit-blocked row into slice 1 the way DR202-RR-F3 says unscoped 'each' would. Defeated by D-002's own parenthetical scoping DR-124's block to its evidence class (M-18).
That the schemas.v6 repoint is stale. It is not — v6 is the lineage head; no v7 exists.

That 'DR-202 F3' inflates an advisory into register standing. Weakened to a citation-precision point inside S-2: file 08's DR-202 row itself states 'F3/F4 remain routed to the DR-111/DR-112 closures', so the route is real at the register.
coordinatorNote: Nothing here asks for the lock rule to be weakened. Both blockers are provenance and disclosure defects sitting on top of substance I could not break. B-1 is the load-bearing one: it is a real misattribution at digest-verified bytes and it lives in the exact sentence the v2 delta exists to repair. B-2 is method rather than content — the undisclosed insertions narrow authority rather than expand it, and a coordinator who weighs that may reasonably downgrade it to SHOULD-FIX; I record it as a blocker because the artifact asks to be reviewed by a bounded diff and then publishes two manifests that do not bound it. Either way the verdict is unchanged: ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX, and S-1 and S-2 stand independently. DR-111 remains OPEN. No implementation is authorized by this verdict.
